uncited: Parametric Function Generation constructs transfer functions by evaluating mathematical functions of a scalar input to determine RGBA output values, rather than relying on piecewise linear interpolation between discrete control points.
It solves the problem of defining smooth, continuous, and often perceptually optimized color mappings with a compact set of parameters.

It differs from its siblings by using explicit analytical formulas (such as cosines, Gaussians, or sigmoids) to define the color space trajectory, offering a global, oscillating, or localized basis for color transitions instead of the local linear segments of [Voxel Color Mapping](2970-voxel-color-mapping.md) or the fixed palettes of [Colormap LUT Generation](7229-colormap-lut-generation.md).
The family shares the mechanism of mapping a normalized scalar input $t \in [0, 1]$ to an RGBA vector $\mathbf{C}$ via a parametric equation.

The input $t$ is typically derived from volume data values normalized to the domain $[0, 1]$ by the parent method [1D Transfer Function Generation and Sampling](2689-1d-transfer-function-generation-and-sampling.md).
where $\mathbf{p}$ represents a set of parameters (vectors or scalars) that control the shape, amplitude, frequency, and phase of the function.
The alpha channel $A$ is often treated separately or derived from the same parametric logic, though in some variants (like Cosine Palette) it is constant or handled by a separate function.
- **Link**: See [Dynamic Focus+Context for Volume Rendering](2689-1d-transfer-function-generation-and-sampling.md) for interaction context.
Parametric function generation in volume rendering transfer functions has evolved from simple piecewise linear interpolation to more sophisticated analytical models.
